title: En route pour l'audition  (On the Way to the Audition)

segments.t: At the ASK reception desk, Gabriel greets his client Sofia Leprince as they prepare for an important casting call. With the audition appointment only minutes away, Sofia asks anxious questions about her character and the script. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Bonjour Gabriel, désolée pour mon retard.
Pose ton sac, on y va!
On est très en retard pour ton audition.
J'ai une seule question sur le texte.
Je n'ai pas lu tout le scénario.
Je ne suis pas sûre du personnage.
C'est une jeune secrétaire jolie et sexy.
Elle croise son patron et décide de le séduire.
Draguer son patron dans une boucherie?
En plus, il pourrait être son père!
Sofia, ne complique pas les choses.
On perd du temps, allons-y maintenant.
D'accord, je suis prête.
Respire et montre ton plus grand sourire.
Let's examine how Gabriel prepares Sofia for her casting session.
Bonjour Gabriel, désolée pour mon retard.
'Hello Gabriel, sorry for my delay.' Sofia apologizes for running late. A handy term meaning sorry is used here in a feminine style to match the speaker. This is perfectly natural in French.
Pose ton sac, on y va!
'Put your bag down, let's go!' Gabriel gives urgent directions. A handy chunk for 'let us go' literally translates as 'we go there'. In French, it works nicely.
On est très en retard pour ton audition.
'We are very late for your audition.' Gabriel uses a casual 'we' instead of the formal version. He adds a handy phrase meaning 'in delay'. The French use this a lot.
J'ai une seule question sur le texte.
'I have just one question about the text.' Sofia asks for clarification. A descriptive term meaning 'only' or 'single' comes right before the idea of a question. In French, it sounds perfect.
Je n'ai pas lu tout le scénario.
'I have not read the entire script.' Sofia admits she is unprepared. The term for a script or screenplay is a cognate you'll easily recognize. This is standard in French.
Je ne suis pas sûre du personnage.
'I am not sure about the character.' Sofia expresses her doubts. She uses a feminine form of a term meaning sure or certain, followed by the concept of a character. A nice sentence in French.
C'est une jeune secrétaire jolie et sexy.
'She is a young, pretty, and sexy secretary.' Gabriel gives a simple summary. He lists three descriptors, two of which are obvious cognates, to outline the role. A great expression in French.
Elle croise son patron et décide de le séduire.
'She runs into her boss and decides to seduce him.' Gabriel summarizes the action. A term meaning to cross paths with someone is followed by the title for a boss. You can say this in French.
Draguer son patron dans une boucherie?
'Hitting on her boss in a butcher shop?' Sofia expresses disbelief. She uses a very common slang term meaning flirting or hitting on someone. In French, this is widely used.
En plus, il pourrait être son père!
'Besides, he could be her father!' Sofia highlights the age difference. A handy expression for 'besides' or 'what is more' literally translates as 'in plus'. The French love this expression.
Sofia, ne complique pas les choses.
'Sofia, do not complicate things.' Gabriel tells her to keep it simple. He starts with a negative command using a core action that means to make complicated. In French, it fits perfectly.
On perd du temps, allons-y maintenant.
'We are wasting time, let us go now.' Gabriel urgently reminds her to leave. He pairs an action meaning to lose or waste with the concept of time. A nice way to say it in French.
D'accord, je suis prête.
'Okay, I am ready.' Sofia confirms she is prepared. She uses a feminine style of the term for ready to match her own gender identity. In French, it is a great choice.
Respire et montre ton plus grand sourire.

'Breathe and show your biggest smile.' Gabriel offers friendly advice. The term for a smile is used here with a descriptor meaning large or big. The French find this natural. Now let's listen to their conversation in the lobby again without pausing.
Bonjour Gabriel, désolée pour mon retard.
Pose ton sac, on y va!
On est très en retard pour ton audition.
J'ai une seule question sur le texte.
Je n'ai pas lu tout le scénario.
Je ne suis pas sûre du personnage.
C'est une jeune secrétaire jolie et sexy.
Elle croise son patron et décide de le séduire.
Draguer son patron dans une boucherie?
En plus, il pourrait être son père!
Sofia, ne complique pas les choses.
On perd du temps, allons-y maintenant.
D'accord, je suis prête.
Respire et montre ton plus grand sourire.
Gabriel rushes Sofia to the casting appointment despite her doubts about the script. See you next time!
À demain!
